conventions: TypeScript strict throughout; formatting is Prettier 2 enforced through eslint-plugin-prettier (80 columns, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas everywhere, 2-space indent); JSON files are Prettier-formatted with printWidth 256.

Import order follows eslint import/order: builtin, external, @excalidraw/** packages after other externals, then parent, then sibling, and `import type` statements last; a blank line between groups; type-only imports are separate `import type { ... }` statements (consistent-type-imports).

Files under packages/element/src import siblings relatively ("./bounds", "./types"); files under packages/excalidraw import runtime code from "@excalidraw/element" and "@excalidraw/common", element types from "@excalidraw/element/types", and never from the "@excalidraw/excalidraw" barrel.

AGENTS.md: derived types use Merge<Base, Overrides> from @excalidraw/common/utility-types, never Omit<...> & {...}; DOM access in new code goes through app.ownerDocument / ownerWindow, never document or window globals.

Scene elements are immutable: a change goes through newElementWith (or scene.mutateElement), which bumps version and versionNonce so history, collab and the render caches see it; a freshly created copy may be adjusted before it is returned.
Render-path helpers (anything getArrowheadPoints, shape generation or getCanvasPadding calls) are constant-time and allocate nothing: no object, array or closure creation per call.
No literal text in JSX: UI strings go through t("labels.<key>") with the English string in packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json only; other locale files are never edited.
An element without arrowheadSize never gains the key: factories, restore and actions write the key only with a valid value, so existing snapshots stay byte-identical.

Tests use vitest globals (describe, it, expect, vi) without importing them, as the existing tests do; jsdom tests render <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} /> in beforeEach, flush with `await act(async () => {})` in afterEach, and drive the editor through window.h, API, UI and Keyboard helpers.
No test adds or rewrites a snapshot (no toMatchSnapshot / toMatchInlineSnapshot); assertions are explicit values, toBeCloseTo for floating point geometry.
Comments are short, lowercase-start, explain why, and match the surrounding style; no TODO comments.

units.behaviour: Scales every arrowhead of an element by its arrowheadSize before the short-segment fitting, makes a large-headed arrow's bounds (and so its export frame) contain its heads, and exports the scale and validation helpers.
rules: 1. Add ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALE and DEFAULT_ARROWHEAD_SIZE to the existing @excalidraw/common import, and ArrowheadSize to the existing `import type { ... } from "./types"`.
2. isArrowheadSize(value) returns `typeof value === "string" && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALE, value)`; it is the only validity test for the field anywhere.

3. getArrowheadSizeScale(element) returns ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALE[DEFAULT_ARROWHEAD_SIZE] when element.arrowheadSize is undefined, ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALE[element.arrowheadSize] when isArrowheadSize accepts it, and ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALE[DEFAULT_ARROWHEAD_SIZE] otherwise; it allocates nothing.
4. Both helpers sit right after getArrowheadSize with a JSDoc line each; getArrowheadSize keeps its signature and values.

5. getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment, cardinality branch: the non-curved result is getArrowheadSize(arrowhead) * Math.min(getArrowheadSizeScale(element), getCardinalityMarkerScale(marker, corner, element.strokeWidth)), so a small marker grows at most to its own size and a large one never past what fits.

6. getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment, case "arrow": `const scale = getArrowheadSizeScale(element);` then legibleSize = (getArrowheadSize(arrowhead) * scale) / 2, and the first getSidesClearSize call takes getArrowheadAngle(arrowhead, legibleSize / scale); the call with angle at size 0 is unchanged.

7. getArrowheadPoints: `const scale = getArrowheadSizeScale(element);` and `const size = getArrowheadSize(arrowhead) * scale;` replace the unscaled size; the fitting below (lengthMultiplier, minSize, getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment) is untouched and so still caps the scaled head on short segments.
8. getArrowheadPoints computes `const angle = getArrowheadAngle(arrowhead, minSize / scale);` so a scaled head keeps the opening angle of the default head at the same relative size.
9. With arrowheadSize absent or "medium" the scale is exactly 1 and every computed value is identical to today.

10. getLinearElementRotatedBounds, right before its final `return coords;` (after the bound-text block, which keeps today's input): when isArrowElement(element) && (element.startArrowhead || element.endArrowhead) && getArrowheadSizeScale(element) > 1, get `const shapes = ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, null);` and, in a for loop from index 1 (no slice), widen coords with `getMinMaxXYFromCurvePathOps(getCurvePathOps(shapes[i]), transformXY)` (min of the minimums, max of the maximums).

11. Rule 10 gets a short comment: heads above the default size overrun the shaft-only bounds and the export padding, so they join the bounds; default and smaller heads keep today's bounds. Absent, medium and small arrows never enter the branch, so their bounds, export frames and snapshots stay byte-identical.

units.behaviour: jsdom tests for the arrowhead size: restore and SVG export, the export frame for large heads, the panel control and undo on the full, compact and mobile layouts, canvas padding, and copy/paste styles.
rules: 1. Imports: pointFrom and type LocalPoint from "@excalidraw/math"; getArrowheadPoints, getCanvasPadding and ShapeCache from "@excalidraw/element"; types from "@excalidraw/element/types"; actionCopyStyles and actionPasteStyles from "../actions/actionStyles"; serializeAsJSON from "../data/json"; restoreElements from "../data/restore"; Excalidraw from "../index"; exportScene from "../scene/export"; API from "./helpers/api"; Keyboard from "./helpers/ui"; act, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor from "./test-utils".

2. `const { h } = window;`; describe("arrowhead size") renders <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} /> in beforeEach and flushes with `await act(async () => {})` in afterEach, as freedrawMode.test.tsx does; a second top-level describe("arrowhead size in compact and mobile panels") has no beforeEach and renders per case, as drawShape.test.tsx's compact toolbar test does.

3. A file-level helper makeArrow(overrides) returns API.createElement({ type: "arrow", x: 0, y: 0, width: 200, height: 0, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(200, 0)], endArrowhead: "arrow", roughness: 0, ...overrides }).

4. A file-level helper getSvgHeadSpread(svg) collects the numbers of every path's d attribute in the exported SVG, takes the odd-indexed ones (y coordinates), and returns max minus min; the shaft is flat, so the spread is the head's width.

5. The scene is set with API.setElements and the selection with API.setSelectedElements; actions run through API.executeAction; undo is Keyboard.undo(); the latest element is read back from h.elements by id.
6. The panel is driven through screen.queryByTestId / getByTestId with the testIds "arrowheadSize-small", "arrowheadSize-medium", "arrowheadSize-large" and fireEvent.click.

7. Head equality in the paste case compares getArrowheadPoints(element, ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, null), "end", "arrow") of target and source with toEqual; both are created with the same points, so only their size can differ.
8. The SVG frame height is Number(svg.getAttribute("height")); exports use no config, so the padding is the default 10px on each side.

9. The compact/mobile case uses it.each(["tablet", "phone"] as const): render <Excalidraw UIOptions={{ getFormFactor: () => formFactor }} />, fireEvent.resize(window), await waitFor until h.app.editorInterface.formFactor is formFactor, set and select the arrow, open the popover with API.setAppState({ openPopup: "compactArrowProperties" }), then await waitFor on the testId query; waitFor comes from "./test-utils" with the other test utilities.
